title: Nuevo Laredo Health Officials Warn of Rising Respiratory Syncytial Virus Cases
excerpt: Health officials in Nuevo Laredo have issued an alert over rising cases of respiratory syncytial virus, urging residents not to brush off early...
content:
Health officials in Nuevo Laredo have issued an alert over a rise in cases of respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV, during the current respiratory illness season, urging residents not to brush off early symptoms.

Filiberto Martínez Cuéllar, an epidemiologist at the city's Hospital General, said RSV is showing a high incidence right now. The situation is not critical at the moment, he said, but the rise has been enough for immunization against the virus to become part of the vaccination card. Health officials are also watching colds, influenza and COVID-19, which require attention as well.

Martínez Cuéllar urged residents to take the first signs of a respiratory illness seriously and seek medical care promptly, rather than waiting to see if symptoms pass on their own.

Residents are advised to protect themselves from the cold with adequate clothing and to keep up a nutrient-rich diet, including vitamins C and A, to support the immune system. Anyone with symptoms should see a doctor, including for a rapid influenza or COVID-19 test when warranted.

The Hospital General de Nuevo Laredo continues to offer medical care and monitoring for respiratory illnesses at its location on Maclovio Herrera 2300, in Colonia Hidalgo.

Sources: El Congresista, Nov. 27, 2026 (with information from Hoy Tamaulipas); Hospital General de Nuevo Laredo.
